key_insight: A room-temperature methylammonium polybromide melt can directly convert elemental metal films into optoelectronic-grade bromide perovskites in a single solvent-free step.
engineering_relevance: This enables lower-complexity, potentially roll-to-roll-compatible manufacturing of perovskite absorber and related films from metals that are otherwise difficult to process.
method: Use methylammonium polybromide melt as a reactive bromide source.
Expose elemental films of Pb, Sn, Au, or Cu to the melt at room temperature.
Tune melt composition to control reactivity and suppress Sn overoxidation.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports successful formation of MAPbBr3, MASnBr3, MA2Au2Br6, and MA2CuBr4, with in situ X-ray diffraction revealing transient intermediates in two cases.
watch_item: Reaction outcomes depend on metal oxidation/disproportionation chemistry, so process control is critical to avoid unwanted overoxidation or phase evolution.
paper_title: A Universal Polybromide Melt Strategy for the Direct Conversion of Metals into Optoelectronic-Grade Bromide Perovskites
